unit: mean absolute error in LogS (log10 mol/L), test split of 2,000 rows
tuned_trees_config: GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=600, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, random_state=42). It won 3-fold GroupKFold CV on the training rows with CV MAE 0.7835, out of 8 configs: (300,3,.1) .830, (300,4,.05) .824, (300,6,.05) .792, (300,6,.1) .796, (600,4,.05) .810, (600,4,.1) .808, (600,6,.03) .787, (600,6,.05) .784. On the same folds the network ensemble's CV MAE was 0.7586.
safe_sentence: On 2,000 test compounds the model never saw in training, our small neural network, written from scratch in JavaScript, predicts water solubility from 17 simple descriptors with an average error of 0.76 log units, which is about a factor of 6 in concentration. Always guessing the average gives 1.92, and a tuned gradient-boosted tree model gives 0.78, so the network is about as good as standard tree methods.
unsafe_sentence: "Our neural network beats gradient-boosted trees by 0.07 log units." That margin only exists against one untuned tree setup. Tuned trees come within 0.016 (95% interval -0.035 to +0.003, which includes zero), and the team's own scaffold split shows a tie (1.00 vs 1.01).
verdict:
The headline number holds and I found no leak. Retraining their trainer on W/nn_data.json with the chosen settings ([96,48], decay 1e-4, huber, 30 epochs, 5 members, seed 11) took 15.9 s. My test predictions match their nn_final.json exactly (largest difference 0.0), and my own MAE is 0.7613 (RMSE 1.117). Naive training-mean MAE is 1.922 and the fixed tree baseline is 0.8344, both matching their numbers.

Leak audit:
(a) Scaling is fit on training rows only (fitScaler and the target mean/sd inside createGenericTrainer): the log1p choice, mean/sd and the clip at +-5 training sd.
(b) No group id appears in both train.g and test.g. No test row shares a SMILES or full InChIKey with a training row. 7 test rows have an input vector identical to a training row; dropping them moves MAE from 0.761 to 0.763. A crude parent-fragment match finds 111 test rows whose parent, as a different salt, mixture or bare form, is in training (an earlier RDKit audit in W/verify/audit.json counted 98). These rows are harder, not easier (network MAE 1.41 on them vs 0.72 on the rest), so they do not flatter the score.
(c) Settings were chosen by grouped 3-fold CV on training rows only (nn_run.js cv mode). Epochs are fixed, there is no early stopping and all 5 members are kept. The extra CV runs (nn_cv_extra.js) used training rows only and were not adopted.
(d) The inputs are the 17 RDKit descriptors only, with no SD, Occurrences, Group or Solubility.
(e) The seeded() function and Mlp class are identical to /workspace/ncsu-hackathon/src/lib/nn.js lines 5-98 apart from one moved comment line. There are no imports beyond node:fs, no trees, no lookup of training labels at prediction time and no pre-trained weights.

The weakness is the comparison. Once the trees are tuned fairly with grouped CV on training rows, they score 0.777 on test against the network's 0.761. The gap is 0.016, and its row-bootstrap 95% interval (-0.035 to +0.003) includes zero. The team's own scaffold split also shows a tie (1.003 vs 1.008), which I did not re-run. Report the network as matching tuned trees, not beating them.
